Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment:  
  - Right knee pain and intermittent clicking for two weeks, worsens with running beyond 2.5-3 miles and gym exercises involving knee flexion-extension; pain localized to center and slightly right side of knee.  
  - Initial mild swelling resolved with ice; currently no swelling or redness.  
  - Full range of motion; no locking or episodes of giving way/instability.  
  - One episode of transient right toe tingling after running; mild pitting edema noted after prolonged standing.  
  - Past minor knee trauma from ice hockey fall months ago likely predisposed to symptoms.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with the transcript and supported by DDx:  
  1. Overuse injury with possible meniscal irritation or patellofemoral pain syndrome (High likelihood) — due to recent increase in running mileage with onset of knee pain, clicking, and no mechanical instability.  
  2. Mild knee inflammation or synovitis (Medium likelihood) — initial mild swelling and response to ice/NSAIDs suggests inflammatory component, though no systemic signs present.  
  3. Mild peripheral neuropathy or nerve irritation (Low to Medium likelihood) — single episode of toe tingling possibly due to mechanical irritation; no persistent neurological deficits.  
  4. Venous insufficiency causing mild lower leg edema (Low likelihood) — sock indentation after standing reported; no DVT signs or knee pain caused by edema.  
  5. Ligamentous injury such as partial ACL or MCL strain (Low to Medium likelihood) — history of trauma supports possibility but absence of instability or mechanical symptoms reduces likelihood.  
- No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx.  

Management Plan  
- Continue ice therapy as currently performed to reduce inflammation.  
- Reduce running intensity/frequency to avoid worsening pain; avoid running through pain requiring stopping.  
- Prescribe stronger anti-inflammatory medication to be taken regularly instead of Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Referral to physiotherapist for detailed knee assessment and management.  
- If physiotherapy wait time is prolonged, arrange clinic appointment for examination.  
- Monitor for urgent symptoms: persistent swelling, heat, redness of knee, fever, feeling unwell, or knee locking with inability to bend/straighten — if these occur, advise urgent medical review.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
- Overuse Injury with possible Meniscal Irritation or Patellofemoral Syndrome (High likelihood): Supported by history of increased running, focal knee pain and clicking without instability.  
- Mild Knee Inflammation or Synovitis (Medium likelihood): Supported by initial swelling responsive to ice/NSAIDs and inflammatory pain pattern.  
- Mild Peripheral Neuropathy or Nerve Irritation (Low to Medium likelihood): Supported by transient toe tingling post-run.  
- Venous Insufficiency or Mild Peripheral Edema (Low likelihood): Supported by mild leg edema on prolonged standing; unlikely primary cause of knee symptoms.  
- Ligamentous Injury (e.g., partial ACL or MCL strain) (Low to Medium likelihood): Trauma history present but no instability or locking argues against major ligament injury.
